- Build a complete, playable rhythm game in the existing project that supports local music files and YouTube videos with automatic beat syncing.

## Requirements
- Create a complete playable game.
- Support uploaded music files.
- Support YouTube video links.
- Include auto-sync functionality.
- Provide desktop and mobile-friendly controls.
- Use reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.

## Decisions
- Built the game as a static HTML/CSS/JavaScript app.
- Used browser-local Web Audio analysis for uploaded-file tempo detection.
- Used a BPM-based chart grid for YouTube sources.
- Included a synthesized 68-second demo track requiring no setup.
- Added keyboard controls with D/F/J/K and touch controls for mobile.

### Completed
- Implemented the complete PULSE rhythm game interface.
- Implemented local audio upload and drag-and-drop.
- Implemented tempo/onset analysis and generated note charts.
- Implemented YouTube URL loading and IFrame API integration.
- Implemented demo playback, scoring, combos, accuracy, pause, restart, and completion states.
- Added responsive desktop and mobile layouts.
- Added an in-page synthesized demo groove and master volume toggle.
- Added chart previews and adjustable BPM/offset settings.
- Verified JavaScript syntax with `node --check`.

### Active
- Final browser capture and visual verification were being prepared.

### Blocked
- No remaining code blocker is known.

## Next Move
1. Run the project and confirm the browser preview renders correctly.
2. Capture desktop and mobile screenshots and inspect them.
3. Exercise demo gameplay and verify note timing, scoring, pause, restart, and finish behavior.
4. Test at least one uploaded audio file and one YouTube URL if network permissions allow.

- `[index.html]`: Complete rhythm game UI, styles, and gameplay implementation.

- The project was implemented as a static app in `index.html`.
- Local audio analysis is performed entirely in the browser and does not upload audio.
- YouTube playback depends on the YouTube IFrame API and browser/embed availability.
- Browser testing had been started with the app served on port 3000.
